title: Notification preference service backed by Redis
name: Notification preference cache

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this service keeps the cache and the database consistent when preferences change? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Which caching strategy does GetAsync implement, and what happens to a user with no row in the database?
choices: Cache-aside: on a miss it loads from the repository, and for an unknown user it caches the default preferences for 30 minutes
Read-through: the cache itself calls the repository, and an unknown user results in a null that is not cached
Cache-aside: on a miss it loads from the repository, but an unknown user is never cached so every call hits the database
Write-behind: the cache is filled first and the repository is updated asynchronously later

questions.prompt: In UpdateAsync, the repository save succeeds and then the Redis SetStringAsync call throws a timeout. What is the resulting state?
choices: Both stores keep the old value because the save is rolled back automatically
The database holds the new preferences, the caller sees an exception, and the cache keeps serving the old value until its entry expires or is overwritten
The database holds the new preferences and the cache holds them too, because IDistributedCache retries internally
The cache holds the new preferences while the database still holds the old ones

questions.prompt: Two requests call GetAsync for the same user on a cold cache at the same moment. What happens?
choices: The second request blocks until the first has populated the cache, so only one database query runs
Redis rejects the second SetStringAsync because the key already exists
Both requests may query the database and both write the same entry; the code does not coordinate them
The second request receives the default preferences instead of waiting
